can_millat_execute.reason: Two blockers below. The classification path is content-capable but under-fed; and there is no Millat extraction input.

blockers.reason: No Millat bbox extraction tables exist (0 found). There is no Millat input to run on.
blockers.note: camelot/pdfplumber available; producing Millat tables is mechanical (not a Millat-specific config). Forbidden to execute in this audit.

blockers.reason: document_context is under-populated: statement_title present on only 204/2113 cells; investee context absent (entity deriver fires 0). So BasisDeriver/EntityScopeDeriver return UNKNOWN for most cells and the Lucky page-range fallback silently classifies them. On Millat the fallback cannot rescue this -> basis ~UNKNOWN (96%), entity_scope UNKNOWN (100%) -> governance collapse.
blockers.note: The derivers are sound; their INPUT signal (page-level statement title + investee-note context) is not captured into the cell. This is the true generalization blocker. Fix = complete the context enrichment to capture page-text title/section/entity context; NOT a Millat-specific rule.

headline: G1 wired deriver-first and preserved Lucky 66/66, but did NOT actually eliminate the page-range dependence: Lucky parity is fallback-driven (basis 96%, entity_scope 100% via Lucky page ranges). Millat is blocked by (B1) missing extraction tables and (B2) incomplete context enrichment that leaves the derivers firing on a small minority. Neither requires a Millat-specific config to fix.
